name: Straight leg raise
movement: both legs straight, one lifted to thirty to forty five degrees and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where your legs will be. The hips and legs are enough: the top half of you can be out of the picture.

words.hint: Lying on your back, both legs straight, one lifted to thirty to forty five degrees.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie on your back side on to it, both legs straight, toes pulled up.
words.position: Lie on your back, side on to the phone, both legs straight and together on the floor, toes pulled up toward you. The camera needs your hips and legs; the rest of you can be out of the picture.
words.top: One straight leg lifted thirty to forty five degrees off the floor, knee locked, toes up, the other leg still flat.
howto: Lie on your back with both legs straight. Pull the toes of both feet toward you.
Tighten the thigh of the working leg so the knee is locked straight, then lift the whole leg to thirty to forty five degrees — about the height of a bent knee.
Hold at the top for the count with the knee straight, the toes up and the other leg flat on the floor.
Lower slowly, keeping the knee straight, until the heel is back on the floor. The rep counts there.
words.cannot: Whether the lower back is flat on the floor and whether the thigh muscle is truly tight: it sees the knee angle, the lift against the other leg and the toes. Press the back down yourself.
words.about: Straight leg raise — lying on your back side on, both legs straight: the lift, as the angle at the hip between the lifted knee and the resting knee, 30–45° at the top — measured against the other leg rather than the floor, so a phone that is not quite level does not move it and the shoulders need not be in the picture (the model reads the two knees 8–15° apart even at rest, so the top allows 48 and the return counts under 15); the lifted knee at least 165° so the leg stays straight; the resting knee at least 160°; and the foot's angle at the heel, 60–105°, toes pulled up. The knee and the toes are coached before the lift is asked for. Hold two seconds at the top, lower slowly, and the rep counts when the heel is down. The toes pulled back and the resting leg straight are coached, but the rep is the knee and the lift: a rep with the toes pointed is counted and told about. With both legs down the far knee hides behind the near one; it then reads as lying on the floor, and the frame is not lost.
words.lost: Lie down side on to the camera, hips and legs in the picture
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: Stop if the lower back or the front of the hip pinches. Press the lower back into the floor; bend the other knee if it will not stay down.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a shorter hold; no weight.
words.harder: A longer hold; an ankle weight; slower lowering.
words.mistakes: The knee bending on the way up; lifting past forty five; toes pointing away; the other leg lifting or bending; the back arching.

measurements.label: knee straight

settings.label: Knee angle, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The knee kept straight: 180 is locked out. Below the band it is bending.

measurements.label: lift off the other leg

settings.label: Lift at the top, at least (degrees)
Lift at the top, at most (degrees)

measurements.why: The angle at the hip between the lifted knee and the resting knee: near 0 with both legs on the floor, 45 lifted forty five. The resting leg is the floor line, so the phone need not be level and the shoulders need not be seen. Also the progress measurement. Side on, the pose model sets the two knees a little apart even with both legs down — a recorded take read 8 to 15 at rest — so the return counts under 15, the lift is under way past 22, and the top allows three degrees past 45 for the same wobble. Side on with both legs down, the far knee is hidden behind the near one and the model stops trusting it (a recorded take read it at 23–43% for six seconds of lying still); a leg the camera cannot see beside its twin is lying on it, so the lift then reads 0 — the start — rather than the frame being lost. It has to be seen for a lift to count, and it is, once the legs part.

measurements.label: resting knee

settings.label: Resting knee, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The other leg stays straight and down: it is the line the lift is measured from. Optional: when the model cannot see it the lift is still read.

measurements.label: toe, heel, knee
measurements.why: The foot against the shin, at the heel: it grows as the toes point away. Toes pulled up keeps the quad working and the knee straight.

faults.label: Knee bending
faults.text: Straighten your knee — tighten the thigh
faults.deep: Lock the knee straight before you lift

faults.label: Toes pointing away
faults.text: Pull your toes up toward you
faults.deep: Toes up — pull the foot back toward you

faults.label: Other knee bending
faults.text: Keep the other leg straight and flat
faults.deep: Press the other leg down straight — it is bending

faults.label: Too high
faults.text: Not so high — forty five at most
faults.deep: Lower it — past forty five degrees

faults.label: Lift short
faults.text: Lift a little higher — thirty degrees at least
faults.deep: Higher — up to between thirty and forty five
